alternatives: pre-position backup power at the highest-load cooling sites
create redundant mobile cooling and welfare-check teams
stage capacity using conservative heat and outage scenarios
assumptions: Heat indicators are aligned to a declared local time zone and spatial support.
Cooling capacity, costs, and response effects remain explicit planning inputs.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: Existing facilities and ordinary surge protocols face the compound event without added redundancy.

constraints.description: Critical cooling and welfare-check functions must remain above the declared minimum continuity level.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: chief resilience officer and public-health incident lead
decision_question: Which continuity portfolio remains feasible under prolonged heat, power loss, and service-demand surge assumptions?

independence_key.binding_constraint: Critical cooling and welfare-check functions must remain above the declared minimum continuity level.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Observed workload and gridded heat inputs retain source lineage while outage and intervention effects remain labeled assumptions.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: multi-hazard Monte Carlo stress testing of facilities and response capacity
independence_key.primary_outcome: scenario-weighted hours of critical service interruption

intended_claim: A versioned stress-test design for comparing declared alternatives affecting compound-heat service-continuity portfolio, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: scenario-weighted hours of critical service interruption
distributional gap in scenario-weighted hours of critical service interruption
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not claim that simulated outages caused observed requests or that a stress test predicts an actual disaster.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.
reference_implementation_note: Tier-D template deep.climate.heat-service-surge.v1 (Heat-context service continuity) supplies a bounded reference workflow for this design axis. The mapping does not establish complete city-specific inputs, external validity, deployment, adoption, or impact.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Observed workload and gridded heat inputs retain source lineage while outage and intervention effects remain labeled assumptions.

title: Stress-test service continuity during compound heat
transportability_risks: Building stock, acclimatization, canopy, humidity, and reporting behavior vary by city.
Thresholds calibrated in one climate zone may not transfer to another.
